Platform stack · Diagram Design

Payments platform · what lives at each tier

Six tiers, thirty-six capabilities, no arrows. Membership and vertical order carry the whole argument: a chip is composed from the tier below it and consumed by the tier above it, and the two full-width bars are the parts there is exactly one of.

THE HEADLINE

One orchestrator, six payment methods

Every method in the payment-core tier reaches the channels through a single orchestrator. That is why it is drawn as a full-width bar rather than a thirteenth chip — and why every method-level outage postmortem ends up in the same code.

Reading the stack

  • Top is nearest the consumer, bottom is outside the platform
  • Full-width bar means there is exactly one
  • Dashed column serves every tier at once
  • Faded chips at the bottom are other people's rails

Why no arrows

Drawing the calls between thirty-six capabilities produces a hairball that answers no question. Adjacency already claims composition; when one specific path matters, it earns its own sequence or data-flow diagram.
